deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the surrounding pages): X is a stratified space, with closed strata X_i indexed by a poset I, so i<=j means X_i is contained in X_j. The open strata are X_i^* = X_i minus its boundary (dot X_i). For i<=k, V_{i,k} is the germ of a closed tubular (regular) neighbourhood of X_i in X_k. V^*_{i,k} is the corresponding deleted neighbourhood (the punctured tube, lying in X_k^*). On the previous page Grothendieck introduced intermediate pieces V^j_{i,k}, for i<=j<=k, by removing from the tube a union of strata R_{j,k} together with S_{j,k}. These interpolate between V^i_{i,k}=V^*_{i,k} and V^k_{i,k}=V_{i,k}. All of them should be (germs of) locally trivial fibrations over X_i^*.

On this page he discusses which of these pieces are good building blocks ('pièces').
(1) When k is an immediate successor of i, the fibre of V_{i,k} over a point z of X_i^* is the normal slice of X_k at z. No stratum lies strictly between X_i and X_k, so this slice has an isolated singularity at z.
(2) For general V^j_{i,k} the fibre can be an arbitrary singularity. Take X_i = X_i^* to be a point: the fibre is then just the germ of X_k at that point. So for non-generic stratifications the general V^j_{i,k} are of limited interest as pieces.
(3) The deleted pieces V^i_{i,k} = V^*_{i,k} are better. Each is essentially a germ of an open part of X_k^* near a singularity, and its fibre over X_i^* is the punctured germ (link) of the normal singularity, roughly V^*_{z,Z_{i,k}}.
(4) Programme: first express as much as possible in terms of the open strata X_i^* and the 'elementary' pieces V_{i,j}, V^*_{i,j}, where j is a successor of i (covering relations of the poset). Then see whether formulas simplify by also allowing all pairs i<j. Only later, mindful of cones and normal sets, see how the intermediate V^j_{i,k} fit in.

The next page carries this out: it bundles the pieces into V_{Δ1} and X^*_{Δ0}, forming a span/quiver diagram indexed by simplices of the nerve of I. This is the start of a description of a stratified space as a diagram of strata and links glued over the nerve of the stratifying poset.
errors: No mathematical error. The 'isolated singularity' claim is correct for the fibre of V_{i,k} when k covers i, if fibre means the normal slice germ. The previous page's definition of S_{j,k}, and the claimed identities R∪S = dot X_k and R∩S = dot X_i, look internally inconsistent (S_{j,k}=X_j for k a successor of j does not match the stated union). That confusion bears on the V^j_{i,k}, which this page sets aside.

ideas.what: Fibres of the tube V_{i,k} over a stratum are normal slices, with an isolated singularity when k covers i; general fibres can be arbitrary singularities (take X_i a point).
ideas.modern_name: Normal slice / local conical structure of Whitney or Thom–Mather stratifications
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 discusses tubular neighbourhoods and dévissage of stratified structures in general terms

ideas.what: Deleted tubular neighbourhoods V^*_{i,k} as basic pieces, fibred over X_i^* with fibre the link of the normal singularity.
ideas.modern_name: Homotopy links (holink) of pairs of strata
ideas.usually_credited_to: Quinn (1988, homotopically stratified sets); later Hughes, Miller

ideas.what: Strategy of describing the stratified space through strata and links attached only to covering pairs (j an immediate successor of i), then to all pairs, then to intermediate pieces; packaged as diagrams indexed by Δ0 and Δ1 of the poset's nerve.
ideas.modern_name: Stratified spaces as diagrams of strata and holinks over the nerve or subdivision of the poset (stratified homotopy hypothesis)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lurie (Higher Algebra, App. A), Douteau, Haine, Douteau–Waas (2010s–2020s)

missed.claim: Grothendieck proposes to express as much of the stratified structure as possible using only strata and links for covering pairs i ⋖ j, extending to all pairs and intermediate pieces only if needed. Modern treatments use links for all flags i0<...<in. Whether, and under what hypotheses, the covering-pair data (plus gluing) suffice is a natural question not explicitly treated there.
missed.quote: essayer d'exprimer le maximum sur les X_i^* et les V_{i,j}, V^*_{i,j} “élémentaires” (j successeur de i)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minimal combinatorial models of stratified homotopy types: reducing flag-indexed holink data to covering-relation data would give smaller presentations (e.g. for computing intersection-type invariants).

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a methodological discussion of which tubular and link pieces to use. It anticipates the modern holink and diagram-over-nerve viewpoint, which is consistent with Esquisse d'un programme. The covering-pair restriction is a mild unpublished detail, not a finished result.
